chinook.text: King salmon usually have black gums at the base of the lower teeth and spots on both tail lobes. Silver salmon have pale gums and usually lack spots on the lower tail lobe.

coho.text: Silver salmon have pale gums at the base of the lower teeth and usually have spots only on the upper tail lobe. King salmon have dark gums and spots on both lobes.

white-sturgeon.text: White sturgeon have barbels closer to the snout tip and at least 36 blunt scutes along the side. Green sturgeon have barbels closer to the mouth and 33 or fewer sharp side scutes.

green-sturgeon.text: Look for barbels nearer the mouth, 33 or fewer sharp side scutes and scutes behind the vent. White sturgeon have more side scutes and barbels nearer the snout tip.

rockfish.text: Compare the lateral line, fin colors and head shape. Similar rockfish can vary in color, especially by age.

Copper rockfish.text: Look for a pale stripe along the rear portion of the lateral line. Use the guide to compare copper, gopher and canary rockfish.

Canary rockfish.text: Look for a pale lateral line and orange patches against a gray body. Compare the head and fin colors with yelloweye.

Yelloweye rockfish.text: Adults have a conspicuous yellow iris. Juveniles can have pale stripes along the side. Use several features before identifying a fish.

Vermilion and sunset rockfish.text: Vermilion and sunset are a cryptic species pair. External features alone cannot reliably distinguish them. The guide compares the group with canary and yelloweye.

south: Common Groundfish of Central and Southern California

Yelloweye.tip: Yellow iris, smooth chin and dark fin edges. Juveniles typically have two pale stripes.

Vermilion/Sunset.tip: Rough chin and upper jaw. These two species cannot reliably be told apart by appearance.

Canary.tip: Gray lateral band, smooth chin and slanted anal fin.

Copper.tip: Pale rear two-thirds of the lateral line. Body color varies.

Gopher.tip: Pink or gray blotches and irregular color along the lateral line.

Quillback.tip: Tall dorsal spines and pale head freckles that usually stop before the tail.

China.tip: Broad yellow band along the lateral line.

Black-and-Yellow.tip: Scattered yellow blotches. No continuous yellow band.

Black.tip: Large mouth, dark mottling and a pale belly.

Blue.tip: Blotched sides, small mouth and jaws that meet when closed.

Yellowtail.tip: Brown flecks, yellow tail and eight soft anal-fin rays.

Olive.tip: Drab olive sides, a longer body and nine soft anal-fin rays.
